quantity: Marionette joint angular range of motion (degrees)
notes: No source found (academic or craft) gives a numeric angular range for marionette shoulder/hip/neck joints. Recommendation: use anatomical human joint ROM (e.g. shoulder flexion ~180deg, abduction ~180deg; hip flexion ~120deg) as an UPPER bound in MuJoCo hinge/ball joint 'range', since a marionette joint is a looser, unstiffened version of the same hinge and is not anatomically restricted the way a living joint is -- but this is a design choice, not a measured number.

No source gives a measured joint damping value. Yamane et al. 2003 fit a per-joint damping term d experimentally but do not report its numeric value in the available text. Recommendation: start from critical damping of each joint's own pendulum mode (see 'Pendulum period' rows below) via MuJoCo's solref dampratio=1 default, then hand-tune down toward underdamped until the 7s swing looks right on screen (per this repo's render-iteration-cache lesson: cache the heavy layers, iterate the cheap joint-damping parameter fast).

Documented explicitly: 'unactuated 2-point tendons with range or springlength of the form [0 X], with positive X... act like a cable, applying force only when stretched' -- this is the exact taut-pulls/slack-does-nothing behaviour asked for, achieved with MuJoCo's native length-limit constraint rather than a manual spring
Default constraint-softness parameters for the tendon LENGTH LIMIT specifically (as opposed to a tendon spring). dampratio=1 = critically damped snap.
Default constraint impedance shape for the tendon length limit
Documented stability requirement; for the default timeconst=0.02s this requires timestep <= 0.01s. MuJoCo's own default timestep (0.002s) already satisfies this 5x over.

quantity: Recommended MuJoCo timestep for this simulation
notes: Not a literature number -- a recommendation synthesized from MuJoCo's documented default (0.002s) and the fact that the drop/snap is a fast transient (see 'free fall time' below, ~0.05-0.09s) that needs several tens of steps to resolve cleanly; if the snap still looks numerically harsh, tighten solreflimit's timeconst toward 2xtimestep rather than shrinking timestep further.

Documented as the recommended default: 'strict improvement' over Euler at similar cost, and stable for systems with tendon/actuator damping, which Euler is not (Euler only integrates JOINT damping implicitly)

quantity: Zimmermann et al. 2019 rigid-link spring constant k
unit: dimensionless (their units, N/m-equivalent in their non-dimensional sim)
notes: k=10^4 used for ALL their body-part rigidity springs (Eq. 19), chosen so body-part deformation is imperceptible; NOT confirmed whether the same k is reused for the string tension term (Eq. 20) -- see caveat in abstracts/zimmermann2019-puppetmaster.txt. Not directly portable to MuJoCo (different formulation/units), but supports 'strings and rigid links should be numerically very stiff relative to gravity/inertia forces' as a design principle.

value: unilateral hard constraint (no stiffness/damping value reported by design)
notes: Explicitly avoids a spring-chain string model, citing numerical stiffness problems; supports using MuJoCo's native length-limit tendon (see above) instead of a manual spring-damper for the strings.

quantity: Free-fall drop height inside the fist
source_file: task brief (design spec, not a literature source)
notes: Given directly in this project's brief, not measured from a source -- kept here only as the input to the free-fall sanity check below.
Standard kinematics, not a citation -- see 'Sanity checks' in the main .md. t=sqrt(2*0.10/9.81)=0.1428s

value: perfectly inelastic collision resolved along each string's own axis (momentum conserved along string; transverse velocity unaffected)
notes: For an idealized massless, perfectly inextensible string suddenly taut: J = m_eff * v_along. In a real (MuJoCo) simulation with finite solref stiffness this idealized instantaneous loss becomes a brief spring-like compression-then-release, which is the physical origin of the small bounce specified in the brief -- not an assumption, a consequence of finite constraint stiffness.

quantity: Marionette limb mass scale (for tension sanity check)
notes: Whole-figure mass for a same-scale (~30cm) robotic marionette; use per-segment fractions from data/02-segment-parameters.csv times an assumed total mass (e.g. 150-300g for a lightweight 'neon' CG figure) to get each limb's mass for the tension/impulse calculation.

For small-angle swinging of a hanging rigid body about a pivot, l = distance from pivot to the body's center of oscillation (~ radius of gyration^2 / distance-to-CM for a physical/compound pendulum, not simply the string length, once the body's own rotational inertia matters).

I_pivot = moment of inertia about the pivot (string attachment/joint), d = distance from pivot to the segment's own center of mass. Use the radius-of-gyration values in data/02-segment-parameters.csv to get I_pivot = m*(k_cg^2 + d^2) via the parallel axis theorem.

quantity: Measured air-drag damping coefficient for an 11.5mm ball pendulum
notes: Smallest ball tested; closest in scale to a marionette hand or head. gamma in x(t)=A*exp(-gamma*t)*cos(omega*t).

quantity: Measured air-drag damping coefficient for a 36.0mm ball pendulum
notes: Largest ball tested, closer in scale to a marionette torso/head. Damping DECREASES with size because mass grows faster than drag.

quantity: Implied log decrement from air drag alone (T~1s)
source_file: computed from salcedo2020 gamma values (delta = gamma*T)
notes: Air resistance alone gives very light damping per swing for a small object -- most of the visible settling over the 7s shot must come from joint/string friction, not air drag. This is a derived sanity check, not a directly reported literature number.
For ball diameters 11.5-36.0mm; proportional to ball radius (low-Reynolds-number/Stokes-like regime), matching the drag equation.

value: t_fall = sqrt(2h/g) should match the number of simulated frames between fist-open and first string-taut event
notes: h = 0.10-0.15m per the brief -> t_fall = 0.143-0.175s (see rows above). If the simulated drop takes noticeably longer or shorter, gravity, initial velocity, or string slack length is wrong.

value: each limb's simulated free-swing period should match T = 2*pi*sqrt(I_pivot/(m*g*d)) computed from its own mass/CG/radius-of-gyration (data/02-segment-parameters.csv)
notes: Compare the MuJoCo-simulated swing period (after a string goes slack and the limb free-swings briefly) to the hand-computed compound-pendulum period for that segment; a large mismatch flags a wrong inertia or CG placement.

value: every string's simulated tendon force should be >= 0 at all times (a string cannot push)
notes: Direct consequence of the unilateral constraint model (Johnson & Murphey 2007; MuJoCo tendon limited=true with stiffness=0 enforces this automatically since the constraint force from a length LIMIT is one-sided by construction).

value: in the settled (static, hanging, non-swinging) pose, the vector sum of all 5 string tensions must equal the total weight of the figure (m_total * g), and the torque sum about the CM must be zero
notes: Standard static-equilibrium check for a multi-string suspension; verify once per settled frame (e.g. the 'card frame' referenced in this project's video-text-fit-check habit) by summing MuJoCo's tendon force sensors.
